newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Radiomobil posts CZK 839 mln 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Czech Radiomobil posts CZK 839 mln 1996 loss.

text.p: Radiomobil a.s., a Czech mobile telephone joint venture managed by a unit of Deutsche Telekom AG, said on Tuesday that it posted a 839 million crown loss for 1996, and expected a larger loss this year.
Gustav Hraska, Radiomobil's financial director, told a news conference that due to heavy investment costs, the company expected a loss of 900 million crowns in 1997.
"Already by 1998 we can be back into black numbers," Hraska said.
He said the losses were primarily due to startup costs of Radiomobil's GSM digital telephone network, Paegas, which was launched in the the third quarter last year.

Radiomobil, which operates one of two Czech GSM digital networks, is comprised 51 percent of Czech transmission company Ceske Radiokomunikace a.s. and 49 percent of an international consortium led by Deutsche Telekom unit DT Mobil.
DT Mobil, which holds more than 80 percent of the consortium's interest in Radiomobil, has assumed the top management positions of the venture.
Radiomobil said its investment had been entirely self-financed in 1996 with two billion crowns in investment made last year, with another 5.3 billion crowns expected in 1997.
Hraska said Radiomobil would soon announce a manadate for an investment bank to arrange a 300 million mark syndicated loan to further its development in 1997.
Radiomobil is in direct competition with Eurotel s.r.o., a joint venture of Czech SPT Telecom a.s., and an American consortium comprised of U.S. West Media Group and Bell Atlantic Corp.
